html:
The Comprehensive Peace Agreement was signed on 9 January 2005 in Nairobi between the government of Sudan and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement, ending the Second Sudanese Civil War.

It was negotiated mostly at Naivasha in Kenya, with pressure from the United States, Britain and Norway and the East African regional body. It gave the south its own government, shared oil revenue and posts in Khartoum, and promised the south a vote on independence after six years.

John Garang became first vice president but died weeks later. The referendum held in January 2011 led to the independence of South Sudan. It ended the second civil war in Sudan.
sum: The Comprehensive Peace Agreement was signed on 9 January 2005 in Nairobi between the government of Sudan and the Sudan People's Liberation Movement, ending the Second Sudanese Civil War.
